clue.text: Identify and eliminate tool, substandard

parts.note: a pick is a digging tool
food or a performance that is off is below par

explanation.surface: A sniper's instruction sheet complains about a shoddy implement.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick off is to single out targets one by one and shoot them down.

clue.text: Take top off the best unguent

explanation.surface: A dairy note: skim the milk, or apply the finest ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together: to cream milk is to skim off its top layer, the cream of anything is its finest part, and a cream is an ointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a dictionary meaning: skim off, the elite, and a soothing lotion.

clue.text: Crowd stock up, according to reports

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the word for stocking up is taken by its sound

parts.note: to hoard is to stockpile supplies

explanation.surface: A news item about shoppers flocking to buy provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large unruly mass of people, a throng.

clue.text: 21 ruler's cat by fireside, tailless

parts.note: the lion is the big cat

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter of the fireplace word is docked

parts.note: the hearth is the floor of a fireplace

explanation.surface: A medieval king's pet curled up by the fire, missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' drops the final H from HEARTH. 21 is ANGEVIN: Richard I, an Angevin king, was called the Lionheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard the Lionheart was a king of the Angevin (Plantagenet) line.

clue.text: Limits set on second cleric's income

indicators.note: set on means the two limits are placed after the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a tip is an extremity or limit
an end is also a limit

explanation.surface: Caps imposed on a junior clergyman's pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' does double work as two separate synonyms placed side by side; 'set on' puts them after the abbreviation, and the definition is the clergyman's pay, not the limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is the fixed salary paid to a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Hard flooring, standard soft one having been removed

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: having been removed says the letter for one is taken out of the soft word

parts.note: quiet means soft in sound
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A flooring fitter replacing a soft standard panel with a harder one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been removed' takes I out of QUIET, leaving QUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquet is flooring made of hardwood blocks laid in a pattern.

clue.text: It stops bats ominously losing old lustre

indicators.note: stops means the word it plugs a gap in the anagrammed letters
bats means crazy, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing says one letter is dropped from the adverb

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something ominously blocks bats from flying, dimming their sheen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' leaves MINOUSLY, 'bats' scrambles it to LUMINOSY, and 'stops' plugs the gap. 'bats' looks like flying mammals but signals the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminosity is brightness or radiance, a sense close to lustre or shine.

clue.text: Magistrate's bill

explanation.surface: A court official's invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is British slang for a magistrate, and a bird's bill is its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: old slang for a judge, and a bird's mouthpart.

clue.text: Men backing promotion course

indicators.note: backing means the abbreviation for men is read in reverse

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: Soldiers supporting a marketing campaign's direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or way, a course to follow.

clue.text: Banter, essentially, if jailbird's confined

indicators.note: confined says the pair of words is enclosed within the Latin phrase

parts.note: per se means in itself or essentially
taken as written
a lag is a convict, an old lag being a habitual prisoner

explanation.surface: Prison chat, which at heart is only possible when the inmate is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confined' encloses the pair within the Latin phrase; the jailbird is a lag, a British slang word for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light mocking talk, essentially banter.

clue.text: A flower some might toast

explanation.surface: A blossom that some people might grill.
explanation.walkthrough: A flower here is something that blooms, and a bloomer is a large crusty British loaf that can be toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that flowers is a bloomer, and a bloomer is also a type of bread loaf.

clue.text: Having no answer, sensitive pressman drew back

indicators.note: having no means the abbreviation for answer is taken out

parts.note: caring means sensitive to others' feelings
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned journalist recoiled, lost for a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no' removes A from CARING, leaving CRING.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to recoil or shrink away in fear or embarrassment.

clue.text: Even so, biography can be a work of art

parts.note: still means nevertheless, even so
a life is a biography

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, a life story can count as art.
explanation.definitionFit: A still life is a painting of inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Agreement to exclude a set of books in which spelling's normal?

definitions.note: a noun phrase: a gathering where casting spells is usual

indicators.note: to exclude says those letters are left out of the agreement word

parts.note: a covenant is a formal agreement
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A treaty leaves out a series of books that use standard spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exclude' removes A and NT from COVENANT. The definition puns on spelling: a coven is a group of witches, who cast spells as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: A coven is a gathering of witches, among whom casting spells is routine.

clue.text: Make good use of maestro when piano's unavailable

indicators.note: unavailable means the letter for piano is missing from the master's word

parts.note: a maestro is a master, an expert
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Make the most of a great conductor when the keyboard can't be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unavailable' drops P from EXPERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert is to bring a power or influence fully into play.

clue.text: Better darts reflecting one way to vary flight

parts.note: to top is to better or surpass

indicators.note: reflecting means the word for darts is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: to nip is to dart quickly

explanation.surface: Advice on improving a darts player's throw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' turns NIPS into SPIN. Darts flights are a red herring: the flight is a ball's path.
explanation.definitionFit: Topspin makes a ball dip in the air, changing its trajectory.

clue.text: Daily forecast about to end

indicators.note: about means the pools word goes round the word for ending

parts.note: a perm is a football pools forecast, a combination of predicted results
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Today's weather prediction is about to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: On the British football pools, a perm (permutation) is a forecast covering several combinations of results.
explanation.definitionFit: Per diem is Latin for 'by the day', so it means daily.

clue.text: Revolutionary marshal raised case of native tribe

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the marshal's name reads upwards

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters of the word native

explanation.surface: A rebel lawman held up the trial of an indigenous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns NEY into YEN; 'case of' takes NE from native.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Drunken contingent from 9, 10 repelled

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the run is read in reverse
a contingent is a part of a larger group, so a run of letters is taken from the two answers

parts.note: the answers to 9 across and 10 across, run together

explanation.surface: A tipsy group from a crowd and a king's army is driven back.
explanation.walkthrough: The answers HORDE and LIONHEART run together hold ORDELIO, which 'repelled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is slang for drunk, well lubricated.

clue.text: Trails wearing of top hats

indicators.note: wearing suggests wear and tear, so the letters are worn into a new order

explanation.surface: Paths followed by people sporting top hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' rearranges OF TOP HATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Footpaths are narrow walking trails.

clue.text: Ambassador admitted to centre to appear consistent

indicators.note: admitted to means the title is let inside the centre word

parts.note: the core is the centre
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat is let into the hub to keep up appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted to' lets the diplomat's title into the centre; HE (His Excellency) is the conventional abbreviation for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hang together logically, to seem consistent.

clue.text: Cancellation inevitable after a long time

indicators.note: after means the certain word follows the period word

parts.note: an era is a long period
sure means certain, bound to happen

explanation.surface: A cancellation was bound to come after so many years.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is a deletion or rubbing out, a cancelling.

clue.text: Vocal work's a wee bit tedious at first

parts.note: a mote is a tiny particle

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of tedious is used

explanation.surface: A choral piece that starts out slightly dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition.

clue.text: Artist's relative turning up at end of game

indicators.note: at end of means the reversed piece comes after the card game

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the abbreviation reads upwards

explanation.surface: A painter's kinsman appears just as the match finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes REL into LER.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American painter.

clue.text: Run through unused plant

parts.note: to spear is to run through with a point
in mint condition means unused

explanation.surface: Impale an untouched shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a garden mint plant.

clue.text: Announcer's calling for treatment from physio, perhaps

indicators.note: an announcer speaks, so the word for requiring is given by its sound

parts.note: calling for means needing

explanation.surface: A broadcaster asks for therapy from a physiotherapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is massage, pressing muscles as a physiotherapist might.

clue.text: A pair of criminals' first botched admission on being arrested?

indicators.note: botched means messed up, so the letters are scrambled
first means just the opening letter of criminals' is used

explanation.surface: Two crooks bungle their first job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges A PAIR OF plus C. 'It's a fair cop' is the stock British confession of a caught criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A fair cop' is the arrested crook's admission that the arrest is justified.

clue.text: A call to restrict possible source of poison

indicators.note: to restrict means the call word hems in the possible word

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness
on means possible or feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A demand to limit a likely poisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' has the call word hem in the possible word; 'on' means possible as in 'that just isn't on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a highly poisonous plant.

clue.text: Evacuated airmen given bubbly from old French province

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, keeping only the outer letters of airmen
bubbly means fizzing, so the letters of given are stirred up

explanation.surface: Pilots who left were handed champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' rearranges GIVEN into GEVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Angevin means of Anjou, a former province of France.

clue.text: Mounted volunteers clutching cross for talisman

indicators.note: clutching means the reversed letters hold the cross inside
mounted in a down clue means the volunteers' letters go upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey

explanation.surface: Cavalry reservists carry a crucifix as a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' turns the volunteers to AT in this down clue, and 'clutching' holds the hybrid animal within; the TA was Britain's Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Time in depot to grease joint?

indicators.note: in means the time letter goes inside the depot word

parts.note: a base is a depot or headquarters

explanation.surface: Time spent in a warehouse to lubricate a coupling.
explanation.walkthrough: The joint is roast meat, not a mechanical joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste a joint of meat is to spoon fat over it while roasting.

clue.text: Shoddy headgear that man's wearing

indicators.note: wearing means the cap goes around the man

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headgear
he is that man

explanation.surface: A man wearing a tatty hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the man in the cap; the wordplay works it as 'that man is wearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap means of poor quality, shoddy.
